questions.stem: The Latin root 'dict' fundamentally means 'to speak' or 'to say'. Based on this, what is the literal historical origin of a 'dictionary'?

options.option_text: A strictly mathematical text containing only silent numbers.
A comprehensive book of spoken words and sayings.
A beautiful collection of colorful hand-painted silent pictures.
A heavy wooden tool used exclusively for building physical structures.

questions.explanation: A 'dictionary' derives from 'dictionarium' (a collection of words/sayings), directly using the root 'dict' (speak/say). It is essentially a comprehensive book of 'things spoken' (words).

questions.stem: The root 'dict' means 'to speak'. If an executive decides to 'dictate' a letter to their secretary, what are they physically doing?

options.option_text: They are secretly throwing the letter directly into the office trash bin.
They are carefully mailing the sealed letter inside a secure postal envelope.
They are speaking the words out loud so another person can write them down.
They are silently reading the letter entirely to themselves in a quiet room.

questions.explanation: To 'dictate' (from 'dictare') means to say or read aloud words to be typed, written down, or recorded by someone or something else. It relies entirely on the root meaning 'to speak'.

questions.stem: Using your knowledge of the root 'dict' (say/speak), what does a weather forecaster do when they 'predict' a storm?

options.option_text: They magically create a storm entirely using ancient powerful spells.
They safely hide underground to escape the incoming dangerous storm.
They desperately ask the government to completely stop the storm.
They explicitly say or state that a storm will happen before it actually occurs.

questions.explanation: To 'predict' combines 'pre-' (before) and 'dict' (speak/say). It literally means 'to say before'. A forecaster predicts a storm by saying it will happen before it actually arrives.

questions.stem: The root 'dict' means 'to speak'. What does it mean if two eyewitnesses fiercely 'contradict' each other in a courtroom?

options.option_text: They speak directly against each other, asserting the complete opposite facts.
They completely agree and say the exact identical story to the judge.
They quietly refuse to speak entirely and remain completely silent.
They physically attack the judge and attempt to flee the courtroom.

questions.explanation: To 'contradict' combines 'contra-' (against) and 'dict' (speak). It literally means 'to speak against'. Eyewitnesses contradict each other when one says the opposite of what the other says.

questions.stem: The root 'dict' means 'say' and 'ver' means 'true'. In a legal trial, what is a 'verdict'?

options.option_text: A deliberate and intentional lie spoken publicly by a guilty criminal.
The specific physical weapon that was heavily used to commit the brutal crime.
The final formal decision of the jury, literally meaning 'true speech' or truth saying.
The incredibly large amount of money paid to easily bail someone completely out of jail.

questions.explanation: A 'verdict' combines 'vere' (truly) and 'dictum' (a saying). In law, it is the finding or decision of a jury on a matter submitted to them in trial, conceptually viewed as 'saying the truth'.

questions.stem: Containing the root 'dict', which formal word describes an official authoritative command, order, or proclamation spoken out heavily by a monarch or government?

options.option_text: evict
edict
elicit
addict

questions.explanation: An 'edict' combines 'e-' (out) and 'dicere' (to say). It literally means something 'spoken out' or proclaimed. Historically, it is an official order or proclamation issued by a person in absolute authority.

questions.stem: The root 'dict' means 'to speak', and 'bene' means 'good'. What is the exact traditional meaning of a 'benediction' at the absolute end of a religious service?

options.option_text: A very harsh 'bad speaking', typically a severe curse placed angrily upon an evil person.
A rapid and silent exit entirely out of the back doors of the church building.
A required financial donation mandatorily collected heavily from everyone entirely present.
A formal utterance of 'good speaking', typically a religious blessing bestowed upon the people.

questions.explanation: A 'benediction' combines 'bene' (well/good) and 'dict' (speak). It literally means 'good speaking' or speaking well of someone, which translates into a religious blessing, especially at the end of a service.
